1	# Hi-C Contact Maps and Distance-Dependent Summaries
2	
3	## Scientific Context
4	
5	Hi-C records pairwise interactions between genomic loci. A contact map divides
6	the genome into intervals and records interaction observations between pairs of
7	intervals. Intrachromosomal pairs can be grouped by genomic separation, which
8	gives a distance-dependent summary commonly used to inspect chromosome folding
9	and to establish a baseline before downstream analyses.
10	
11	A Cooler archive separates genomic-bin information from interaction pixels.
12	The bin table may contain additional annotations created during later processing
13	steps, while the pixel table stores the archived interactions themselves. A
14	scientific workflow must therefore distinguish a malformed archive from a valid
15	archive that simply carries a different set of available annotations.
16	
17	Distance-dependent contact summaries are usually reported across a broad range
18	of separations. Log-distance smoothing is one common presentation technique for
19	making broad trends readable. A completed analysis should remain a finite,
20	interpretable tabular result rather than failing merely because an archive came
21	from a different stage of a research pipeline.
22	
23	## Method and Format Sources
24	
25	The following primary and official materials provide the scientific and data
26	format background for this task. They are references, not a diagnosis of the
27	historical implementation failure.
28	
29	- Abdennur et al. *Cooltools: Enabling High-Resolution Hi-C Analysis in
30	  Python.* bioRxiv, 2022.
31	  [doi:10.1101/2022.10.31.514564](https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.10.31.514564).
32	- Lieberman-Aiden et al. *Comprehensive Mapping of Long-Range Interactions
33	  Reveals Folding Principles of the Human Genome.* Science, 2009.
34	  [doi:10.1126/science.1181369](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1181369).
35	- [Cooler data-model concepts](https://cooler.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts.html),
36	  covering the bin and pixel tables in Cooler HDF5 contact maps.
37	- [Cooltools contacts-versus-distance tutorial](https://cooltools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebooks/contacts_vs_distance.html)
38	  and [CLI reference](https://cooltools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/cli.html),
39	  covering project workflows for contact-map summaries.
40	
41	The supplied source snapshot contains the version-specific command help and

29	def lattice_pdist_frequencies(n, points):
30	    """
31	    Distribution of pairwise 1D distances among a collection of distinct
32	    integers ranging from 0 to n-1.
33	
34	    Parameters
35	    ----------
36	    n : int
37	        Size of the lattice on which the integer points reside.
38	    points : sequence of int
39	        Arbitrary integers between 0 and n-1, inclusive, in any order but
40	        with no duplicates.
41	
42	    Returns
43	    -------
44	    h : 1D array of length n
45	        h[d] counts the number of integer pairs that are exactly d units apart
46	
47	    Notes
48	    -----
49	    This is done using a convolution via FFT. Thanks to Peter de Rivaz; see
50	    `<http://stackoverflow.com/questions/42423823/distribution-of-pairwise-distances-between-many-integers>`_.
51	
52	    """
53	    if len(np.unique(points)) != len(points):
54	        raise ValueError("Integers must be distinct.")
55	    x = np.zeros(n)
56	    x[points] = 1
57	    return np.round(fftconvolve(x, x[::-1], mode="full")).astype(int)[-n:]

60	def count_bad_pixels_per_diag(n, bad_bins):
61	    """
62	    Efficiently count the number of bad pixels on each upper diagonal of a
63	    matrix assuming a sequence of bad bins forms a "grid" of invalid pixels.
64	
65	    Each bad bin bifurcates into two a row and column of bad pixels, so an
66	    upper bound on number of bad pixels per diagonal is 2*k, where k is the
67	    number of bad bins. For a given diagonal, we need to subtract from this
68	    upper estimate the contribution from rows/columns reaching "out-of-bounds"
69	    and the contribution of the intersection points of bad rows with bad
70	    columns that get double counted.
71	
72	    ::
73	
74	        o : bad bin
75	        * : bad pixel
76	        x : intersection bad pixel
77	        $ : out of bounds bad pixel
78	             $    $     $
79	         *--------------------------+
80	          *  *    *     *           |
81	           * *    *     *           |
82	            **    *     *           |
83	             o****x*****x***********|$
84	              *   *     *           |
85	               *  *     *           |
86	                * *     *           |
87	                 o******x***********|$
88	                  *     *           |
89	                   *    *           |
90	                    *   *           |
91	                     *  *           |
92	                      * *           |
93	                       **           |
94	                        o***********|$
95	                         *          |
96	                          *         |
97	
98	    Parameters
99	    ----------
100	    n : int
101	        total number of bins
102	    bad_bins : 1D array of int
103	        sorted array of bad bin indexes
104	
105	    Returns
106	    -------
107	    dcount : 1D array of length n
108	        dcount[d] == number of bad pixels on diagonal d
109	
110	    """
111	    k = len(bad_bins)
112	    dcount = np.zeros(n, dtype=int)
113	
114	    # Store all intersection pixels in a separate array
115	    # ~O(n log n) with fft
116	    ixn = lattice_pdist_frequencies(n, bad_bins)
117	    dcount[0] = ixn[0]
118	
119	    # Keep track of out-of-bounds pixels by squeezing left and right bounds
120	    # ~O(n)
121	    pl = 0
122	    pr = k
123	    for diag in range(1, n):
124	        if pl < k:
125	            while (bad_bins[pl] - diag) < 0:
126	                pl += 1
127	                if pl == k:
128	                    break
129	        if pr > 0:
130	            while (bad_bins[pr - 1] + diag) >= n:
131	                pr -= 1
132	                if pr == 0:
133	                    break
134	        dcount[diag] = 2 * k - ixn[diag] - pl - (k - pr)
135	    return dcount

157	    """
158	    Calculate total number of pixels in a rectangular block

161	    ----------
162	    x : int
163	        block width in pixels
164	    y : int

175	def count_bad_pixels_per_block(x, y, bad_bins_x, bad_bins_y):
176	    """
177	    Calculate number of "bad" pixels per rectangular block of a contact map
178	
179	    Parameters
180	    ----------
181	    x : int
182	        block width in pixels
183	    y : int
184	        block height in pixels
185	    bad_bins_x : int
186	        number of bad bins on x-side
187	    bad_bins_y : int
188	        number of bad bins on y-side
189	
190	    Returns
191	    -------
192	    number_of_pixes : int
193	        number of "bad" pixels in a block
194	    """
195	
196	    # Calculate the resulting bad pixels in a rectangular block:
197	    return (x * bad_bins_y) + (y * bad_bins_x) - (bad_bins_x * bad_bins_y)

200	def make_diag_table(bad_mask, span1, span2):
201	    """
202	    Compute the total number of elements ``n_elem`` and the number of bad
203	    elements ``n_bad`` per diagonal for a single contact area encompassing
204	    ``span1`` and ``span2`` on the same genomic scaffold (cis matrix).
205	
206	    Follows the same principle as the algorithm for finding contact areas for
207	    computing scalings.
208	
209	    Parameters
210	    ----------
211	    bad_mask : 1D array of bool
212	        Mask of bad bins for the whole genomic scaffold containing the regions
213	        of interest.
214	    span1, span2 : pair of ints
215	        The bin spans (not genomic coordinates) of the two regions of interest.
216	
217	    Returns
218	    -------
219	    diags : pandas.DataFrame
220	        Table indexed by 'diag' with columns ['n_elem', 'n_bad'].
221	
222	    """
223	
224	    # alias for np.flatnonzero inside `make_diag_table`
225	    where = np.flatnonzero
226	
227	    def _make_diag_table(n_bins, bad_locs):
228	        diags = pd.DataFrame(index=pd.Series(np.arange(n_bins), name=_DIST))
229	        diags["n_elem"] = count_all_pixels_per_diag(n_bins)
230	        diags[_NUM_VALID] = diags["n_elem"] - count_bad_pixels_per_diag(
231	            n_bins, bad_locs
232	        )
233	        return diags
234	
235	    if span1 == span2:
236	        lo, hi = span1
237	        diags = _make_diag_table(hi - lo, where(bad_mask[lo:hi]))
238	    else:
239	        lo1, hi1 = span1
240	        lo2, hi2 = span2
241	        if lo2 <= lo1:
242	            lo1, lo2 = lo2, lo1
243	            hi1, hi2 = hi2, hi1
244	        diags = (
245	            _make_diag_table(hi2 - lo1, where(bad_mask[lo1:hi2]))
246	            .subtract(
247	                _make_diag_table(lo2 - lo1, where(bad_mask[lo1:lo2])), fill_value=0
248	            )
249	            .subtract(
250	                _make_diag_table(hi2 - hi1, where(bad_mask[hi1:hi2])), fill_value=0
251	            )
252	        )
253	        if hi1 < lo2:
254	            diags.add(
255	                _make_diag_table(lo2 - hi1, where(bad_mask[hi1:lo2])), fill_value=0
256	            )
257	        diags = diags[diags["n_elem"] > 0]
258	
259	    diags = diags.drop("n_elem", axis=1)
260	    return diags.astype(int)

263	def make_diag_tables(clr, regions, regions2=None, clr_weight_name="weight"):
264	    """
265	    For every region infer diagonals that intersect this region and calculate
266	    the size of these intersections in pixels, both "total" and "n_valid",
267	    where "n_valid" does not count "bad" pixels.
268	
269	    "Bad" pixels are inferred from the balancing weight column `clr_weight_name`.
270	    When `clr_weight_name` is None, raw data is used, and no "bad" pixels are exclued.
271	
272	    When `regions2` are provided, all intersecting diagonals are reported for
273	    each rectangular and asymmetric block defined by combinations of matching
274	    elements of `regions` and `regions2`.
275	    Otherwise only `regions`-based symmetric square blocks are considered.
276	    Only intra-chromosomal regions are supported.
277	
278	    Parameters
279	    ----------
280	    clr : cooler.Cooler
281	        Input cooler
282	    regions : viewframe or viewframe-like dataframe
283	        viewframe without repeated entries or viewframe-like dataframe with repeated entries
284	    regions2 : viewframe or viewframe-like dataframe
285	        viewframe without repeated entries or viewframe-like dataframe with repeated entries
286	    clr_weight_name : str
287	        name of the weight column in the clr bin-table,
288	        Balancing weight is used to infer bad bins, set to
289	        `None` is masking bad bins is not desired for raw data.
290	
291	    Returns
292	    -------
293	    diag_tables : dict
294	        dictionary with DataFrames of relevant diagonals for every region.
295	    """
296	
297	    try:  # Run regular viewframe conversion:
298	        regions = bioframe.make_viewframe(
299	            regions, check_bounds=clr.chromsizes
300	        ).to_numpy()
301	        if regions2 is not None:
302	            regions2 = bioframe.make_viewframe(
303	                regions2, check_bounds=clr.chromsizes
304	            ).to_numpy()
305	    except ValueError:  # If there are non-unique entries in regions1/2, possible only for asymmetric expected:
306	        regions = pd.concat(
307	            [
308	                bioframe.make_viewframe([region], check_bounds=clr.chromsizes)
309	                for i, region in regions.iterrows()
310	            ]
311	        ).to_numpy()
312	        regions2 = pd.concat(
313	            [
314	                bioframe.make_viewframe([region], check_bounds=clr.chromsizes)
315	                for i, region in regions2.iterrows()
316	            ]
317	        ).to_numpy()
318	
319	    bins = clr.bins()[:]
320	    if clr_weight_name is None:
321	        # ignore bad bins
322	        sizes = dict(bins.groupby("chrom").size())
323	        bad_bin_dict = {
324	            chrom: np.zeros(sizes[chrom], dtype=bool) for chrom in sizes.keys()
325	        }
326	    elif is_cooler_balanced(clr, clr_weight_name):
327	        groups = dict(iter(bins.groupby("chrom")[clr_weight_name]))
328	        bad_bin_dict = {
329	            chrom: np.array(groups[chrom].isnull()) for chrom in groups.keys()
330	        }
331	    else:
332	        raise ValueError(
333	            f"provided cooler is not balanced, or weight {clr_weight_name} is missing"
334	        )
335	
336	    diag_tables = {}
337	    for i, region in enumerate(regions):
338	        chrom, start1, end1, name1 = region
339	        if regions2 is not None:
340	            chrom2, start2, end2, name2 = regions2[i]
341	            # cis-only for now:
342	            if not (chrom2 == chrom):
343	                raise ValueError(
344	                    "regions/2 have to be on the same chrom to generate diag_tables"
345	                )
346	        else:
347	            start2, end2 = start1, end1
348	
349	        # translate regions into relative bin id-s:
350	        lo1, hi1 = clr.extent((chrom, start1, end1))
351	        lo2, hi2 = clr.extent((chrom, start2, end2))
352	        co = clr.offset(chrom)
353	        lo1 -= co
354	        lo2 -= co
355	        hi1 -= co
356	        hi2 -= co
357	
358	        bad_mask = bad_bin_dict[chrom]
359	        newname = name1
360	        if regions2 is not None:
361	            newname = (name1, name2)
362	        diag_tables[newname] = make_diag_table(bad_mask, [lo1, hi1], [lo2, hi2])
363	
364	    return diag_tables

367	def make_block_table(clr, regions1, regions2, clr_weight_name="weight"):
368	    """
369	    Creates a table of total and valid pixels for a set of rectangular genomic blocks
370	    defined by regions1 and regions2.
371	    For every block calculate its "area" in pixels ("n_total"), and calculate
372	    number of "valid" pixels ("n_valid").
373	    Valid pixels exclude "bad" pixels, which are inferred from the balancing
374	    weight column `clr_weight_name`.
375	
376	    When `clr_weight_name` is None, raw data is used, and no "bad" pixels are exclued.
377	
378	    Parameters
379	    ----------
380	    clr : cooler.Cooler
381	        Input cooler
382	    regions1 : viewframe-like dataframe
383	        viewframe-like dataframe, where repeated entries are allowed
384	    regions2 : viewframe-like dataframe
385	        viewframe-like dataframe, where repeated entries are allowed
386	    clr_weight_name : str
387	        name of the weight column in the cooler bins-table, used
388	        for masking bad pixels.
389	        When clr_weight_name is None, no bad pixels are masked.
390	
391	    Returns
392	    -------
393	    block_table : dict
394	        dictionary for blocks that are 0-indexed
395	    """
396	
397	    try:  # Run regular viewframe conversion:
398	        regions1 = bioframe.make_viewframe(
399	            regions1, check_bounds=clr.chromsizes
400	        ).to_numpy()
401	        regions2 = bioframe.make_viewframe(
402	            regions2, check_bounds=clr.chromsizes
403	        ).to_numpy()
404	    except ValueError:  # Might be non-unique entries in regions:
405	        regions1 = pd.concat(
406	            [
407	                bioframe.make_viewframe([region], check_bounds=clr.chromsizes)
408	                for i, region in regions1.iterrows()
409	            ]
410	        ).to_numpy()
411	        regions2 = pd.concat(
412	            [
413	                bioframe.make_viewframe([region], check_bounds=clr.chromsizes)
414	                for i, region in regions2.iterrows()
415	            ]
416	        ).to_numpy()
417	
418	    # should we check for nestedness here, or that each region1 is < region2 ?
419	
420	    block_table = {}
421	    for r1, r2 in zip(regions1, regions2):
422	        chrom1, start1, end1, name1 = r1
423	        chrom2, start2, end2, name2 = r2
424	        # translate regions into relative bin id-s:
425	        lo1, hi1 = clr.extent((chrom1, start1, end1))
426	        lo2, hi2 = clr.extent((chrom2, start2, end2))
427	        # width and height of a block:
428	        x = hi1 - lo1
429	        y = hi2 - lo2
430	
431	        # now we need to combine it with the balancing weights
432	        if clr_weight_name is None:
433	            bad_bins_x = 0
434	            bad_bins_y = 0
435	        elif is_cooler_balanced(clr, clr_weight_name):
436	            # count "bad" bins filtered by balancing:
437	            bad_bins_x = clr.bins()[clr_weight_name][lo1:hi1].isnull().sum()
438	            bad_bins_y = clr.bins()[clr_weight_name][lo2:hi2].isnull().sum()
439	        else:
440	            raise ValueError(
441	                f"cooler is not balanced or weight {clr_weight_name} is missing"
442	            )
443	
444	        # calculate total and bad pixels per block:
445	        n_tot = count_all_pixels_per_block(x, y)
446	        n_bad = count_bad_pixels_per_block(x, y, bad_bins_x, bad_bins_y)
447	
448	        # fill in "block_table" with number of valid pixels:
449	        block_table[name1, name2] = {_NUM_VALID: n_tot - n_bad}
450	
451	    return block_table

454	def _diagsum_symm(clr, fields, transforms, clr_weight_name, regions, span):
455	    """
456	    calculates diagonal/distance summary for a collection of
457	    square symmetric blocks defined by the "regions".
458	
459	    Return:
460	    dictionary of DataFrames with diagonal/distance
461	    sums for the "fields", and 0-based indexes of square
462	    genomic regions as keys.
463	    """
464	    lo, hi = span
465	    bins = clr.bins()[:]
466	    pixels = clr.pixels()[lo:hi]
467	    pixels = cooler.annotate(pixels, bins, replace=False)
468	    # pre-filter cis-only pixels to speed up calculations
469	    pixels = pixels[pixels["chrom1"] == pixels["chrom2"]].copy()
470	
471	    # annotate pixels with regions at once
472	    # book-ended regions still get reannotated
473	    pixels["r1"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="1")
474	    pixels["r2"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="2")
475	    # select symmetric pixels that have notnull weights
476	    if clr_weight_name is None:
477	        pixels = pixels.dropna(subset=["r1", "r2"])
478	    else:
479	        pixels = pixels.dropna(
480	            subset=["r1", "r2", clr_weight_name + "1", clr_weight_name + "2"]
481	        )
482	    pixels = pixels[pixels["r1"] == pixels["r2"]]
483	
484	    # this could further expanded to allow for custom groupings:
485	    pixels[_DIST] = pixels["bin2_id"] - pixels["bin1_id"]
486	    for field, t in transforms.items():
487	        pixels[field] = t(pixels)
488	
489	    symm_blocks = pixels.groupby("r1")
490	    return {int(i): block.groupby(_DIST)[fields].sum() for i, block in symm_blocks}

493	def diagsum_symm(
494	    clr,
495	    view_df,
496	    transforms={},
497	    clr_weight_name="weight",
498	    ignore_diags=2,
499	    chunksize=10000000,
500	    map=map,
501	):
502	    """
503	
504	    Intra-chromosomal diagonal summary statistics.
505	
506	    Parameters
507	    ----------
508	    clr : cooler.Cooler
509	        Cooler object
510	    view_df : viewframe
511	        view_dfof regions for intra-chromosomal diagonal summation
512	    transforms : dict of str -> callable, optional
513	        Transformations to apply to pixels. The result will be assigned to
514	        a temporary column with the name given by the key. Callables take
515	        one argument: the current chunk of the (annotated) pixel dataframe.
516	    clr_weight_name : str
517	        name of the balancing weight vector used to count "bad"
518	        pixels per diagonal. Set to `None` not to mask
519	        "bad" pixels (raw data only).
520	    chunksize : int, optional
521	        Size of pixel table chunks to process
522	    ignore_diags : int, optional
523	        Number of intial diagonals to exclude from statistics
524	    map : callable, optional
525	        Map functor implementation.
526	
527	    Returns
528	    -------
529	    Dataframe of diagonal statistics for all regions in the view
530	
531	    """
532	    spans = partition(0, len(clr.pixels()), chunksize)
533	    fields = list(chain(["count"], transforms))
534	    # names of summary results
535	    summary_fields = [f"{field}.sum" for field in fields]
536	
537	    # check viewframe
538	    try:
539	        _ = is_compatible_viewframe(
540	            view_df,
541	            clr,
542	            check_sorting=False,  # liberal for this low-level function
543	            raise_errors=True,
544	        )
545	    except Exception as e:
546	        raise ValueError("provided view_df is not valid") from e
547	
548	    # prepare dtables: for every region a table with diagonals, number of valid pixels, etc
549	    dtables = make_diag_tables(clr, view_df, clr_weight_name=clr_weight_name)
550	
551	    # initialize columns to store summary results in dtables
552	    for dt in dtables.values():
553	        for agg_name in summary_fields:
554	            dt[agg_name] = 0

586	def _diagsum_pairwise(clr, fields, transforms, clr_weight_name, regions, span):
587	    """
588	    calculates diagonal/distance summary for a collection of
589	    rectangular blocks defined by all pairwise combinations
590	    of "regions" for intra-chromosomal interactions.
591	
592	    Return:
593	    dictionary of DataFrames with diagonal/distance
594	    sums for the "fields", and (i,j)-like indexes of rectangular
595	    genomic regions as keys.

597	    lo, hi = span
598	    bins = clr.bins()[:]
599	    pixels = clr.pixels()[lo:hi]
600	    pixels = cooler.annotate(pixels, bins, replace=False)
601	    # pre-filter cis-only pixels to speed up calculations
602	    pixels = pixels[pixels["chrom1"] == pixels["chrom2"]].copy()
603	
604	    # annotate pixels with regions at once
605	    # book-ended regions still get reannotated
606	    pixels["r1"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="1")
607	    pixels["r2"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="2")
608	    # pre-filter asymetric pixels only that have notnull weights
609	    if clr_weight_name is None:
610	        pixels = pixels.dropna(subset=["r1", "r2"])
611	    else:
612	        pixels = pixels.dropna(
613	            subset=["r1", "r2", clr_weight_name + "1", clr_weight_name + "2"]
614	        )
615	    # pixels = pixels[ pixels["r1"] != pixels["r2"] ]
616	
617	    # this could further expanded to allow for custom groupings:
618	    pixels[_DIST] = pixels["bin2_id"] - pixels["bin1_id"]
619	    for field, t in transforms.items():

621	
622	    asymm_blocks = pixels.groupby(["r1", "r2"])

736	def _blocksum_pairwise(clr, fields, transforms, clr_weight_name, regions, span):
737	    """
738	    calculates block summary for a collection of
739	    rectangular regions defined as pairwise combinations
740	    of all regions.
741	
742	    Return:
743	    a dictionary of block-wide sums for all "fields":
744	    keys are (i,j)-like, where i and j are 0-based indexes of
745	    "regions", and a combination of (i,j) defines rectangular block.
746	
747	    Note:
748	    Input pixels are assumed to be "symmetric-upper", and "regions"
749	    to be sorted according to the order of chromosomes in "clr", thus
750	    i < j.
751	
752	    """
753	    lo, hi = span
754	    bins = clr.bins()[:]
755	    pixels = clr.pixels()[lo:hi]
756	    pixels = cooler.annotate(pixels, bins, replace=False)
757	
758	    pixels["r1"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="1")
759	    pixels["r2"] = assign_supports(pixels, regions, suffix="2")
760	    # pre-filter asymetric pixels only that have notnull weights
761	    if clr_weight_name is None:
762	        pixels = pixels.dropna(subset=["r1", "r2"])
763	    else:
764	        pixels = pixels.dropna(
765	            subset=["r1", "r2", clr_weight_name + "1", clr_weight_name + "2"]
766	        )
767	    pixels = pixels[pixels["r1"] != pixels["r2"]]
768	
769	    # apply transforms, e.g. balancing etc
770	    for field, t in transforms.items():
771	        pixels[field] = t(pixels)
772	
773	    # pairwise-combinations of regions define asymetric pixels-blocks
774	    pixel_groups = pixels.groupby(["r1", "r2"])
775	    return {
776	        (int(i), int(j)): group[fields].sum(skipna=False)
777	        for (i, j), group in pixel_groups
778	    }

786	    chunksize=1000000,

792	
793	    Note
794	    ----

797	    once and pixels falling into a given asymmetric block i != j are summed up.

815	        Size of pixel table chunks to process
816	    map : callable, optional

822	
823	    """
824	
825	    # check viewframe
826	    try:
827	        _ = is_compatible_viewframe(
828	            view_df,
829	            clr,

844	    regions1 = pd.DataFrame(regions1)
845	    regions2 = pd.DataFrame(regions2)
846	    # similar with diagonal summations, pre-generate a block_table listing
847	    # all of the rectangular blocks and "n_valid" number of pixels per each block:
848	    btables = make_block_table(clr, regions1, regions2, clr_weight_name=clr_weight_name)
849	
850	    # initialize columns to store summary results in btables
851	    for bt in btables.values():
852	        for agg_name in summary_fields:
853	            bt[agg_name] = 0
854	
855	    # apply _diagsum_pairwise to chunks of pixels
856	    job = partial(
857	        _blocksum_pairwise, clr, fields, transforms, clr_weight_name, view_df.to_numpy()

881	def expected_cis(
882	    clr,
883	    view_df=None,
884	    intra_only=True,
885	    smooth=True,
886	    aggregate_smoothed=True,
887	    smooth_sigma=0.1,
888	    clr_weight_name="weight",
889	    ignore_diags=2,  # should default to cooler info
890	    chunksize=10_000_000,
891	    nproc=1,
892	    map_functor=map,
893	):
894	    """
895	    Calculate average interaction frequencies as a function of genomic
896	    separation between pixels i.e. interaction decay with distance.
897	    Genomic separation aka "dist" is measured in the number of bins,
898	    and defined as an index of a diagonal on which pixels reside (bin1_id - bin2_id).
899	
900	    Average values are reported in the columns with names {}.avg, and they
901	    are calculated as a ratio between a corresponding sum {}.sum and the
902	    total number of "valid" pixels on the diagonal "n_valid".
903	
904	    When balancing weights (clr_weight_name=None) are not applied to the data, there is no
905	    masking of bad bins performed.
906	
907	
908	    Parameters
909	    ----------
910	    clr : cooler.Cooler
911	        Cooler object
912	    view_df : viewframe
913	        a collection of genomic intervals where expected is calculated
914	        otherwise expected is calculated for full chromosomes.
915	        view_df has to be sorted, when inter-regions expected is requested,
916	        i.e. intra_only is False.
917	    intra_only: bool
918	        Return expected only for symmetric intra-regions defined by view_df,
919	        i.e. chromosomes, chromosomal-arms, intra-domains, etc.
920	        When False returns expected both for symmetric intra-regions and
921	        assymetric inter-regions.
922	    smooth: bool
923	        Apply smoothing to cis-expected. Will be stored in an additional column
924	    aggregate_smoothed: bool
925	        When smoothing, average over all regions, ignored without smoothing.
926	    smooth_sigma: float
927	        Control smoothing with the standard deviation of the smoothing Gaussian kernel.
928	        Ignored without smoothing.
929	    clr_weight_name : str or None
930	        Name of balancing weight column from the cooler to use.
931	        Use raw unbalanced data, when None.
932	    ignore_diags : int, optional
933	        Number of intial diagonals to exclude results
934	    chunksize : int, optional
935	        Size of pixel table chunks to process
936	    nproc : int, optional
937	        How many processes to use for calculation. Ignored if map_functor is passed.
938	    map_functor : callable, optional
939	        Map function to dispatch the matrix chunks to workers.
940	        If left unspecified, pool_decorator applies the following defaults: if nproc>1 this defaults to multiprocess.Pool;
941	        If nproc=1 this defaults the builtin map. 
942	
943	    Returns
944	    -------
945	    DataFrame with summary statistic of every diagonal of every symmetric
946	    or asymmetric block:
947	    region1, region2, diag, n_valid, count.sum count.avg, etc
948	
949	    """
950	
951	    if view_df is None:
952	        if not intra_only:
953	            raise ValueError(
954	                "asymmetric regions has to be smaller then full chromosomes, use view_df"
955	            )
956	        else:
957	            # Generate viewframe from clr.chromsizes:
958	            view_df = make_cooler_view(clr)
959	    else:
960	        # Make sure view_df is a proper viewframe
961	        try:
962	            _ = is_compatible_viewframe(
963	                view_df,
964	                clr,
965	                # must be sorted for asymmetric case
966	                check_sorting=(not intra_only),
967	                raise_errors=True,
968	            )
969	        except Exception as e:
970	            raise ValueError("view_df is not a valid viewframe or incompatible") from e
971	
972	    # define transforms - balanced and raw ('count') for now
973	    if clr_weight_name is None:
974	        # no transforms
975	        transforms = {}
976	    elif is_cooler_balanced(clr, clr_weight_name):
977	        # define balanced data transform:
978	        weight1 = clr_weight_name + "1"
979	        weight2 = clr_weight_name + "2"
980	        transforms = {"balanced": lambda p: p["count"] * p[weight1] * p[weight2]}
981	
982	    else:
983	        raise ValueError(
984	            "cooler is not balanced, or"
985	            f"balancing weight {clr_weight_name} is not available in the cooler."
986	        )
987	
988	    # using try-clause to close mp.Pool properly
989	    if intra_only:
990	        result = diagsum_symm(
991	            clr,
992	            view_df,
993	            transforms=transforms,
994	            clr_weight_name=clr_weight_name,
995	            ignore_diags=ignore_diags,
996	            chunksize=chunksize,
997	            map=map_functor,
998	        )
999	    else:
1000	        result = diagsum_pairwise(
1001	            clr,
1002	            view_df,
1003	            transforms=transforms,
1004	            clr_weight_name=clr_weight_name,
1005	            ignore_diags=ignore_diags,
1006	            chunksize=chunksize,
1007	            map=map_functor,
1008	        )
1009	
1010	    # calculate actual averages by dividing sum by n_valid:
1011	    for key in chain(["count"], transforms):
1012	        result[f"{key}.avg"] = result[f"{key}.sum"] / result[_NUM_VALID]
1013	
1014	    # additional smoothing and aggregating options would add columns only, not replace them
1015	    if smooth:
1016	        result_smooth = expected_smoothing.agg_smooth_cvd(
1017	            result,
1018	            sigma_log10=smooth_sigma,
1019	        )
1020	        # add the smoothed result to the per-region table
1021	        result = result.merge(
1022	            result_smooth[["balanced.avg.smoothed", _DIST]],
1023	            on=[_REGION1, _REGION2, _DIST],

1029	                groupby=None,

1031	            ).rename(columns={"balanced.avg.smoothed": "balanced.avg.smoothed.agg"})

1033	            result = result.merge(
1034	                result_smooth_agg[["balanced.avg.smoothed.agg", _DIST]],
1035	                on=[
1036	                    _DIST,
1037	                ],
1038	                how="left",
1039	            )
1040	
1041	    return result

1148	
1149	    return result

1152	def diagsum_from_array(
1153	    A, counts=None, *, offset=0, ignore_diags=2, filter_counts=False, region_name=None
1154	):
1155	    """
1156	    Calculates Open2C-formatted expected for a dense submatrix of a whole
1157	    genome contact map.
1158	
1159	    Parameters
1160	    ----------
1161	    A : 2D array
1162	        Normalized submatrix to calculate expected (``balanced.sum``).
1163	    counts : 2D array or None, optional
1164	        Corresponding raw contacts to populate ``count.sum``.
1165	    offset : int or (int, int)
1166	        i- and j- bin offsets of A relative to the parent matrix. If a single
1167	        offset is provided it is applied to both axes.
1168	    ignore_diags : int, optional
1169	        Number of initial diagonals to ignore.
1170	    filter_counts : bool, optional
1171	        Apply the validity mask from balanced matrix to the raw one. Ignored
1172	        when counts is None.
1173	    region_name : str or (str, str), optional
1174	        A custom region name or pair of region names. If provided, region
1175	        columns will be included in the output.
1176	
1177	    Notes
1178	    -----
1179	    For regions that cross the main diagonal of the whole-genome contact map,
1180	    the lower triangle "overhang" is ignored.
1181	
1182	    Examples
1183	    --------
1184	    >>> A = clr.matrix()[:, :]  # whole genome balanced
1185	    >>> C = clr.matrix(balance=False)[:, :]  # whole genome raw
1186	
1187	    Using only balanced data:
1188	    >>> exp = diagsum_from_array(A)
1189	
1190	    Using balanced and raw counts:
1191	    >>> exp1 = diagsum_from_array(A, C)
1192	
1193	    Using an off-diagonal submatrix
1194	    >>> exp2 = diagsum_from_array(A[:50, 50:], offset=(0, 50))
1195	
1196	    """
1197	    if isinstance(offset, (list, tuple)):
1198	        offset1, offset2 = offset
1199	    else:
1200	        offset1, offset2 = offset, offset
1201	    if isinstance(region_name, (list, tuple)):
1202	        region1, region2 = region_name
1203	    elif region_name is not None:
1204	        region1, region2 = region_name, region_name
1205	    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float)
1206	    if counts is not None:
1207	        counts = np.asarray(counts)
1208	        if counts.shape != A.shape:
1209	            raise ValueError("`counts` must have the same shape as `A`.")
1210	
1211	    # Compute validity mask for bins on each axis
1212	    invalid_mask1 = np.sum(np.isnan(A), axis=1) == A.shape[0]
1213	    invalid_mask2 = np.sum(np.isnan(A), axis=0) == A.shape[1]
1214	
1215	    A[~np.isfinite(A)] = 0
1216	
1217	    # Prepare an indicator matrix of "diagonals" (toeplitz) where the lower
1218	    # triangle diagonals wrt the parent matrix are negative.
1219	    # The "outer difference" operation below produces a toeplitz matrix.
1220	    lo1, hi1 = offset1, offset1 + A.shape[0]
1221	    lo2, hi2 = offset2, offset2 + A.shape[1]
1222	    ar1 = np.arange(lo1, hi1, dtype=np.int32)
1223	    ar2 = np.arange(lo2, hi2, dtype=np.int32)
1224	    diag_indicator = ar2[np.newaxis, :] - ar1[:, np.newaxis]
1225	    diag_lo = max(lo2 - hi1 + 1, 0)
1226	    diag_hi = hi2 - lo1
1227	
1228	    # Apply the validity mask to the indicator matrix.
1229	    # Both invalid and lower triangle pixels will now have negative indicator values.
1230	    D = diag_indicator.copy()
1231	    D[invalid_mask1, :] = -1
1232	    D[:, invalid_mask2] = -1
1233	    # Drop invalid and lower triangle pixels and flatten.
1234	    mask_per_pixel = D >= 0
1235	    A_flat = A[mask_per_pixel]
1236	    D_flat = D[mask_per_pixel]
1237	
1238	    # Group by diagonal and aggregate the number of valid pixels and pixel values.
1239	    diagonals = np.arange(diag_lo, diag_hi, dtype=int)
1240	    n_valid = np.bincount(D_flat, minlength=diag_hi - diag_lo)[diag_lo:]
1241	    balanced_sum = np.bincount(D_flat, weights=A_flat, minlength=diag_hi - diag_lo)[
1242	        diag_lo:
1243	    ]
1244	    # Mask to ignore initial diagonals.
1245	    mask_per_diag = diagonals >= ignore_diags
1246	
1247	    # Populate the output dataframe.
1248	    # Include region columns if region names are provided.
1249	    # Include raw pixel counts for each diag if counts is provided.
1250	    df = pd.DataFrame({_DIST: diagonals, _NUM_VALID: n_valid})
1251	
1252	    if region_name is not None:
1253	        df.insert(0, _REGION1, region1)
1254	        df.insert(1, _REGION2, region2)
1255	
1256	    if counts is not None:
1257	        # Either count everything or apply the same filtering as A.
1258	        if filter_counts:
1259	            C_flat = counts[mask_per_pixel]
1260	            count_sum = np.bincount(
1261	                D_flat, weights=C_flat, minlength=diag_hi - diag_lo
1262	            )[diag_lo:]
1263	        else:
1264	            mask_per_pixel = diag_indicator >= 0
1265	            D_flat = diag_indicator[mask_per_pixel]
1266	            C_flat = counts[mask_per_pixel]
1267	            count_sum = np.bincount(
1268	                D_flat, weights=C_flat, minlength=diag_hi - diag_lo
1269	            )[diag_lo:]
1270	        count_sum[~mask_per_diag] = np.nan
1271	        df["count.sum"] = count_sum
1272	
1273	    balanced_sum[~mask_per_diag] = np.nan
1274	    df["balanced.sum"] = balanced_sum
1275	
1276	    return df

1279	def logbin_expected(
1280	    exp,
1281	    summary_name="balanced.sum",
1282	    bins_per_order_magnitude=10,
1283	    bin_layout="fixed",
1284	    smooth=lambda x: numutils.robust_gauss_filter(x, 2),
1285	    min_nvalid=200,
1286	    min_count=50,
1287	):
1288	    """
1289	    Logarithmically bins expected as produced by diagsum_symm method.
1290	
1291	    Parameters
1292	    ----------
1293	    exp : DataFrame
1294	        DataFrame produced by diagsum_symm
1295	
1296	    summary_name : str, optional
1297	        Name of the column of exp-DataFrame to use as a diagonal summary.
1298	        Default is "balanced.sum".
1299	
1300	    bins_per_order_magnitude : int, optional
1301	        How many bins per order of magnitude. Default of 10 has a ratio of
1302	        neighboring bins of about 1.25
1303	
1304	    bin_layout : "fixed", "longest_region", or array
1305	        "fixed" means that bins are exactly the same for different datasets,
1306	        and only depend on bins_per_order_magnitude
1307	
1308	        "longest_region" means that the last bin will end at size of the
1309	        longest region.
1310	            GOOD: the last bin will have as much data as possible.
1311	            BAD: bin edges will end up different for different datasets, you
1312	            can't divide them by each other
1313	
1314	        array: provide your own bin edges. Can be of any size, and end at any
1315	        value. Bins exceeding the size of the largest region will be simply
1316	        ignored.
1317	
1318	    smooth : callable
1319	        A smoothing function to be applied to log(P(s)) and log(x)
1320	        before calculating P(s) slopes for by-region data
1321	
1322	    min_nvalid : int
1323	        For each region, throw out bins (log-spaced) that have less than
1324	        min_nvalid valid pixels
1325	        This will ensure that each entree in Pc_by_region has at least n_valid
1326	        valid pixels
1327	        Don't set it to zero, or it will introduce bugs. Setting it to 1 is OK,
1328	        but not recommended.
1329	
1330	    min_count : int
1331	        If counts are found in the data, then for each region, throw out bins
1332	        (log-spaced)
1333	        that have more than min_counts of counts.sum (raw Hi-C counts).
1334	        This will ensure that each entree in Pc_by_region has at least
1335	        min_count raw Hi-C reads
1336	
1337	    Returns
1338	    -------
1339	    Pc : DataFrame
1340	        dataframe of contact probabilities and spread across regions
1341	    slope : ndarray
1342	        slope of Pc(s) on a log-log plot and spread across regions
1343	    bins : ndarray
1344	        an array of bin edges used for calculating P(s)
1345	
1346	    Notes
1347	    -----
1348	    For main Pc and slope, the algorithm is the following
1349	
1350	    1. concatenate all the expected for all regions into a large dataframe.
1351	    2. create logarithmically-spaced bins of diagonals (or use provided)
1352	    3. pool together n_valid and balanced.sum for each region and for each bin
1353	    4. calculate the average diagonal for each bucket, weighted by n_valid
1354	    5. divide balanced.sum by n_valid after summing for each bucket (not before)
1355	    6. calculate the slope in log space (for each region)
1356	
1357	    X values are not midpoints of bins
1358	    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1359	    In step 4, we calculate the average diag index weighted by n_valid. This
1360	    seems counter-intuitive, but it actually is justified.
1361	
1362	    Let's take the worst case scenario. Let there be a bin from 40MB to 44MB.
1363	    Let there be a region that is exactly 41 MB long. The midpoint of the bin
1364	    is at 42MB. But the only part of this region belonging to this bin is
1365	    actually between 40MB and 41MB. Moreover, the "average" read in this
1366	    little triangle of the heatmap is actually not coming even from 40.5 MB
1367	    because the triangle is getting narrower towards 41MB. The center of mass
1368	    of a triangle is 1/3 of the way up, or 40.33 MB. So an average read for
1369	    this region in this bin is coming from 40.33.
1370	
1371	    Consider the previous bin, say, from 36MB to 40MB. The heatmap there is a
1372	    trapezoid with a long side of 5MB, the short side of 1MB, and height of
1373	    4MB. The center of mass of this trapezoid is at 36 + 14/9 = 37.55MB,
1374	    and not at 38MB. So the last bin center is definitely mis-assigned, and
1375	    the second-to-last bin center is off by some 25%. This would lead to a 25%
1376	    error of the P(s) slope estimated between the third-to-last and
1377	    second-to-last bin.
1378	
1379	    In presence of missing bins, this all becomes more complex, but this kind
1380	    of averaging should take care of everything. It follows a general
1381	    principle: when averaging the y values with some weights, one needs to
1382	    average the x values with the same weights. The y values here are being
1383	    added together, so per-diag means are effectively averaged with the weight
1384	    of n_valid. Therefore, the x values (diag) should be averaged with the
1385	    same weights.
1386	
1387	    Other considerations
1388	    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1389	    Steps #3 and #5 are important because the ratio of sums does not equal to
1390	    the sum of ratios, and the former is more correct (the latter is more
1391	    susceptible to noise). It is generally better to divide at the very end,
1392	    rather than dividing things for each diagonal.
1393	
1394	    Here we divide at the end twice: first we divide balanced.sum by n_valid
1395	    for each region, then we effectively multiply it back up and divide it for
1396	    each bin when combining different regions (see weighted average in the
1397	    next function).
1398	
1399	    Smoothing P(s) for the slope
1400	    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1401	    For calcuating the slope, we apply smoothing to the P(s) to ensure the
1402	    slope is not too noisy. There are several caveats here: the P(s) has to
1403	    be smoothed in logspace, and both P and s have to be smoothed. It is
1404	    discussed in detail here
1405	
1406	    https://gist.github.com/mimakaev/4becf1310ba6ee07f6b91e511c531e73
1407	
1408	    Examples
1409	    --------
1410	    For example, see this gist: https://gist.github.com/mimakaev/e9117a7fcc318e7904702eba5b47d9e6
1411	
1412	    """
1413	
1414	    def _get_diag_bins(bin_layout, diagmax, bins_per_order_magnitude):
1415	        """
1416	        create the logbins themselves based on layout, maxdiag, etc.
1417	        """
1418	        # create diag_bins based on chosen layout:
1419	        if bin_layout == "fixed":
1420	            diag_bins = numutils.persistent_log_bins(
1421	                10, bins_per_order_magnitude=bins_per_order_magnitude
1422	            )
1423	        elif bin_layout == "longest_region":
1424	            diag_bins = numutils.logbins(
1425	                1, diagmax + 1, ratio=10 ** (1 / bins_per_order_magnitude)
1426	            )
1427	        elif isinstance(bin_layout, np.ndarray):
1428	            diag_bins = bin_layout
1429	        else:
1430	            raise ValueError("bin_layout can be fixed, longest_region or an ndarray")
1431	
1432	        if diag_bins[-1] < diagmax:
1433	            raise ValueError(
1434	                "Genomic separation bins end is less than the size of the largest region"
1435	            )
1436	        return diag_bins
1437	
1438	    def _get_weighted_expected(
1439	        exp_filtered,
1440	        diag_bins,
1441	        digit_id_name,
1442	        weighted_dist_name,
1443	        Pc_name,
1444	        summary_name,
1445	        raw_summary_name,
1446	        min_nvalid=0,
1447	        min_count=0,
1448	    ):
1449	        """
1450	        given the logbins (diag_bins) and expected with digitized distances (and pre-filtered)
1451	        calculate weighted distance per logbin and weighted expected.
1452	        """
1453	
1454	        # digitize dist: assign diagonals in expected df to diag_bins, - give them ids:
1455	        exp_filtered[digit_id_name] = (
1456	            np.searchsorted(diag_bins, exp_filtered[weighted_dist_name], side="right")
1457	            - 1
1458	        )
1459	        exp_filtered = exp_filtered[
1460	            exp_filtered[digit_id_name] >= 0
1461	        ]  # ignore those that do not fit into diag_bins
1462	
1463	        # constructing expected grouped by region
1464	        byReg = exp_filtered.copy()
1465	
1466	        # this averages diag_avg with the weight equal to n_valid, and sums everything else
1467	        byReg[weighted_dist_name] *= byReg[_NUM_VALID]  # dist * n_valid
1468	        byRegExp = byReg.groupby(
1469	            [_REGION1, _REGION2, digit_id_name]
1470	        ).sum()  # sum in each logbin
1471	        byRegExp[weighted_dist_name] /= byRegExp[
1472	            _NUM_VALID
1473	        ]  # sum(dist*n_valid) / sum(n_valid)
1474	
1475	        byRegExp = byRegExp.reset_index()
1476	        byRegExp = byRegExp[byRegExp[_NUM_VALID] > min_nvalid]  # filtering by n_valid
1477	        byRegExp[Pc_name] = byRegExp[summary_name] / byRegExp[_NUM_VALID]
1478	        byRegExp = byRegExp[byRegExp[Pc_name] > 0]  # drop diag_bins with 0 counts
1479	        # try to filter by the matching raw number of interactions
1480	        if min_count:
1481	            if raw_summary_name in byRegExp:
1482	                byRegExp = byRegExp[byRegExp[raw_summary_name] > min_count]
1483	            else:
1484	                warnings.warn(
1485	                    RuntimeWarning(
1486	                        f"{raw_summary_name} not found in the input expected"
1487	                    )
1488	                )
1489	
1490	        byRegExp["dist_bin_start"] = diag_bins[byRegExp[digit_id_name].to_numpy()]
1491	        byRegExp["dist_bin_end"] = diag_bins[byRegExp[digit_id_name].to_numpy() + 1] - 1
1492	
1493	        return byRegExp

1495	    def _get_slopes(
1496	        logbin_exp,
1497	        digit_id_name,
1498	        weighted_dist_name,
1499	        Pc_name,
1500	    ):
1501	        """
1502	        calculate derivative of P(s) (our logbinned weighted average expected)
1503	        """
1504	
1505	        slope_name = "slope"
1506	
1507	        # now calculate P(s) derivatives aka slopes per region
1508	        byRegDer = []
1509	        for (reg1, reg2), subdf in logbin_exp.groupby([_REGION1, _REGION2]):
1510	            subdf = subdf.sort_values(digit_id_name)
1511	            valid = np.minimum(
1512	                subdf[_NUM_VALID].to_numpy()[:-1], subdf[_NUM_VALID].to_numpy()[1:]
1513	            )
1514	            # geometric mean of each logbin - aka mids
1515	            mids = np.sqrt(
1516	                subdf[weighted_dist_name].to_numpy()[:-1]
1517	                * subdf[weighted_dist_name].to_numpy()[1:]
1518	            )
1519	            slope = np.diff(smooth(np.log(subdf[Pc_name].to_numpy()))) / np.diff(
1520	                smooth(np.log(subdf[weighted_dist_name].to_numpy()))
1521	            )
1522	            newdf = pd.DataFrame(
1523	                {
1524	                    weighted_dist_name: mids,
1525	                    slope_name: slope,
1526	                    _NUM_VALID: valid,
1527	                    digit_id_name: subdf[digit_id_name].to_numpy()[:-1],
1528	                }
1529	            )
1530	            newdf[_REGION1] = reg1
1531	            newdf[_REGION2] = reg2
1532	            byRegDer.append(newdf)
1533	        byRegDer = pd.concat(byRegDer).reset_index(drop=True)
1534	
1535	        return byRegDer
1536	
1537	    raw_summary_name = "count.sum"
1538	    exp_summary_base, *_ = summary_name.split(".")
1539	    Pc_name = f"{exp_summary_base}.avg"
1540	    diag_name = _DIST
1541	    diag_avg_name = f"{diag_name}.avg"
1542	    # filter expected from NaNs in summary column and copy (precaution)
1543	    exp = exp.dropna(
1544	        subset=[
1545	            summary_name,
1546	        ]
1547	    ).copy()
1548	    # rename "dist" column dist.avg, it'll change later
1549	    exp[diag_avg_name] = exp.pop(diag_name)
1550	
1551	    # generate the "logbins", i.e. uneven bins for the diagonal distances
1552	    diag_bins = _get_diag_bins(
1553	        bin_layout=bin_layout,
1554	        diagmax=exp[diag_avg_name].max(),
1555	        bins_per_order_magnitude=bins_per_order_magnitude,
1556	    )
1557	    # assign distances to logbins and calculate weight averages for dist and counts
1558	    byRegExp = _get_weighted_expected(
1559	        exp,
1560	        diag_bins,
1561	        digit_id_name="dist_bin_id",
1562	        weighted_dist_name=diag_avg_name,
1563	        Pc_name=f"{exp_summary_base}.avg",
1564	        summary_name=summary_name,
1565	        raw_summary_name="count.sum",
1566	        min_nvalid=min_nvalid,
1567	        min_count=min_count,
1568	    )
1569	
1570	    # now calculate P(s) derivatives aka slopes per region
1571	    byRegDer = _get_slopes(
1572	        byRegExp,
1573	        digit_id_name="dist_bin_id",
1574	        weighted_dist_name=diag_avg_name,
1575	        Pc_name=f"{exp_summary_base}.avg",
1576	    )
1577	
1578	    # returning logbin expected, its derivative and lobins themselves:
1579	    return byRegExp, byRegDer, diag_bins[: byRegExp["dist_bin_id"].max() + 2]

1582	def combine_binned_expected(
1583	    binned_exp,
1584	    binned_exp_slope=None,
1585	    Pc_name="balanced.avg",
1586	    der_smooth_function_combined=lambda x: numutils.robust_gauss_filter(x, 1.3),
1587	    spread_funcs="logstd",
1588	    spread_funcs_slope="std",
1589	    minmax_drop_bins=2,
1590	    concat_original=False,
1591	):
1592	    """
1593	    Combines by-region log-binned expected and slopes into genome-wide averages,
1594	    handling small chromosomes and "corners" in an optimal fashion, robust to
1595	    outliers. Calculates spread of by-chromosome P(s) and slopes, also in an optimal fashion.
1596	
1597	    Parameters
1598	    ----------
1599	    binned_exp: dataframe
1600	        binned expected as outputed by logbin_expected
1601	
1602	    binned_exp_slope : dataframe or None
1603	        If provided, estimates spread of slopes.
1604	        Is necessary if concat_original is True
1605	
1606	    Pc_name : str
1607	        Name of the column with the probability of contacts.
1608	        Defaults to "balanced.avg".
1609	
1610	    der_smooth_function_combined : callable
1611	        A smoothing function for calculating slopes on combined data
1612	
1613	    spread_funcs: "minmax", "std", "logstd" or a function (see below)
1614	        A way to estimate the spread of the P(s) curves between regions.
1615	        * "minmax" - use the minimum/maximum of by-region P(s)
1616	        * "std" - use weighted standard deviation of P(s) curves (may produce negative results)
1617	        * "logstd" (recommended) weighted standard deviation in logspace (as seen on the plot)
1618	
1619	    spread_funcs_slope: "minmax", "std" or a funciton
1620	        Similar to spread_func, but for slopes rather than P(s)
1621	
1622	    concat_original: bool (default = False)
1623	        Append original dataframe, and put combined under region "combined"
1624	
1625	    Returns
1626	    -------
1627	    scal, slope_df
1628	
1629	    Notes
1630	    -----
1631	    This function does not calculate errorbars. The spread is not the deviation of the mean,
1632	    and rather is representative of variability between chromosomes.
1633	
1634	
1635	    Calculating errorbars/spread
1636	
1637	    1. Take all by-region P(s)
1638	    2. For "minmax", remove the last var_drop_last_bins bins for each region
1639	       (by default two. They are most noisy and would inflate the
1640	       spread for the last points). Min/max are most susceptible to this.
1641	    3. Groupby P(s) by region
1642	    4. Apply spread_funcs to the pd.GroupBy object. Options are:
1643	       * minimum and maximum ("minmax"),
1644	       * weighted standard deviation ("std"),
1645	       * weighted standard deviation in logspace ("logstd", default) or two custom functions
1646	       We do not remove the last bins for "std" / "logstd" because we are
1647	       doing weighted standard deviation. Therefore, noisy "ends" of regions
1648	       would contribute very little to this.
1649	    5. Append them to the P(s) for the same bin.
1650	
1651	    As a result, by for minmax, we do not estimate spread for the last
1652	    two bins. This is because there are often very few chromosomal arms there,
1653	    and different arm measurements are noisy. For other methods, we do
1654	    estimate the spread there, and noisy last bins are taken care of by the
1655	    weighted standard deviation. However, the spread in the last bins may be
1656	    noisy, and may become a 0 if only one region is contributing to the last
1657	    pixel.
1658	    """
1659	    diag_avg_name = f"{_DIST}.avg"
1660	    # combine pre-logbinned expecteds
1661	    scal = numutils.weighted_groupby_mean(
1662	        binned_exp[
1663	            [
1664	                Pc_name,
1665	                "dist_bin_id",
1666	                "n_valid",
1667	                diag_avg_name,
1668	                "dist_bin_start",
1669	                "dist_bin_end",
1670	            ]
1671	        ],
1672	        group_by="dist_bin_id",
1673	        weigh_by="n_valid",
1674	        mode="mean",
1675	    )
1676	
1677	    # for every diagonal calculate the spread of expected
1678	    if spread_funcs == "minmax":
1679	        byRegVar = binned_exp.copy()
1680	        byRegVar = byRegVar.loc[

def _resolve_cvd_cols(cvd, cols=None):
    """
    Resolve the column mapping used for contact-vs-distance smoothing.

    The standard mapping describes a balanced contact table, but a valid
    cooler may lack bin-level balancing annotations. In that case the
    workflow provides raw contact summaries instead. If the requested
    contact-frequency columns are not present, fall back to the equivalent

    if (
